name: is.epc/mcp
title: epc.is EPCIS Repository
description: EPCIS 2.0 repository: trace products, query and count events, resolve GS1 Digital Links.

tools.name: checkEpcisConformance
tools.description:
Score an EPCIS document across every conformance dimension at once, including whether it
used the identifiers it was given. Use this as a final self-check before presenting a
document to a user.

Pass suppliedText as what the user actually told you, verbatim — their whole request is
fine. This is the only way to detect a FABRICATED identifier, which passes every other
check and yet describes a different physical object. Leave it empty only when the user
genuinely supplied nothing.

suppliedText.description: What the user told you, verbatim

tools.name: describeCbvTerm
tools.description:
Get the CBV's own definition of a term, and its example of use. Use this to confirm that
a term means what you think before putting it in a document — the definitions are the
standard's text, not a paraphrase.

field.description: The event field: bizStep, disposition, bizTransactionType, sourceType/destinationType

tools.name: digitalLinkToUrn
tools.description: Convert a GS1 Digital Link URI into the legacy EPC URN form. Supply the GCP (company prefix) length if you know it; pass 0 to let the resolver determine it. Only use URNs when the user explicitly asks for them — Digital Link is the preferred form.

gcpLength.description: GCP length, or 0 to determine it automatically

tools.name: dpp
tools.description: The Digital Product Passport of a product, Lot or Serial by its GS1 Digital Link, from the DPP API (EN 18223 structure). Read with the user's sign-in, so the fields their access tier allows are included. representation: compressed (default), operational, full, gs1 or eu.

identifier.description: the product's GS1 Digital Link, e.g. https://id.epc.is/01/09523001010089

representation.description: compressed (default), operational, full, gs1 or eu

tools.name: findCbvTerms
tools.description:
Find candidate CBV terms for an EPCIS event field by matching words from a description
of what happened. Returns the terms whose names share a word stem with the description,
most specific first, or the whole list when nothing matches.

This is a NAME match, not a semantic one: it narrows the choice, it does not make it.
Two terms can both look plausible for the same sentence — `collecting` and `receiving`
are the known example — and only the CBV definitions settle that. Read the returned
candidates as a shortlist to reason about, and prefer being explicit with the user over
guessing between near-synonyms.

field.description: The event field: bizStep, disposition, bizTransactionType, sourceType/destinationType

description.description: What happened, in words, e.g. "items picked for an order"

tools.name: get_event
tools.description: One EPCIS event by its eventID, exactly as the repository holds it (JSON-LD), for the signed-in user.

eventId.description: the eventID, e.g. ni:///sha-256;...?ver=CBV2.0 or urn:uuid:...

tools.name: links
tools.description: The full GS1 Digital Link linkset of an identifier: every link type the resolver serves for it (product passport, master data, EPCIS repository, instructions and so on), with titles and languages.

tools.name: listCbvTerms
tools.description:
List every standard CBV term for an EPCIS event field. Use this instead of recalling
terms from memory — the list is small, closed, and generated from the CBV standard, and
a term that is not on it will be rejected when the document is captured.

field.description: The event field: bizStep, disposition, bizTransactionType, sourceType/destinationType

tools.name: listDocumentIdentifiers
tools.description:
List the identifiers an EPCIS document actually uses, grouped by the field that carries
them. Use this to check at a glance that a document is about the objects and places you
intended, without reading the whole JSON.

tools.name: masterdata
tools.description: What the GS1 Digital Link resolver knows about a product (GTIN, Lot, Serial), a place (GLN, SGLN) or a party (PGLN): name, description, brand, location and the like, as the platform publishes it.

identifier.description: a GS1 Digital Link, e.g. https://id.epc.is/01/09523001010089 or /414/<gln>

tools.name: query_events
tools.description: Query the EPCIS 2.0 repository as the signed-in user, who sees exactly what their account may read. Filters are EPCIS Query Language parameters; every one is optional and they are AND-ed, several values of one comma-separated are OR-ed. Identifiers are GS1 Digital Links (https://id.gs1.org/01/<gtin>/21/<serial>, /10/<lot>, /00/<sscc>, /414/<gln>/254/<ext>) or EPC URNs. Answers one page, newest first, each event compact with its eventID; pass nextPage back for more.

eventType.description: ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransformationEvent, AssociationEvent or TransactionEvent

bizStep.description: CBV bizStep, bare (shipping) or as URI

disposition.description: CBV disposition, bare (in_transit) or as URI

epc.description: an instance or class identifier anywhere in the event (MATCH_anyEPC / MATCH_anyEPCClass)

readPoint.description: Read Point, an SGLN Digital Link (EQ_readPoint)

bizLocation.description: Business Location, an SGLN Digital Link (EQ_bizLocation)

from.description: events at or after this time, ISO 8601 (GE_eventTime)

more.description: further EPCIS query parameters as a query string, e.g. EQ_bizTransaction_po=urn:...&EXISTS_mc:orderLines=true

limit.description: events on this page, 1 to the server's page size

nextPage.description: the nextPage of a previous answer; the other filters are then ignored

tools.name: summarize
tools.description: Count the signed-in user's EPCIS events, computed by the repository in one call, grouped by one dimension: eventType, bizStep, disposition, readPoint, bizLocation, action, day or month. Takes the same filters as query_events. Use it for "how many", "which steps", "per day" questions instead of paging through events; then query_events for the events behind a bucket.

groupBy.description: eventType, bizStep, disposition, readPoint, bizLocation, action, day or month

eventType.description: ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransformationEvent, AssociationEvent or TransactionEvent

bizStep.description: CBV bizStep, bare (shipping) or as URI

disposition.description: CBV disposition, bare (in_transit) or as URI

epc.description: an instance or class identifier anywhere in the event

readPoint.description: Read Point, an SGLN Digital Link

bizLocation.description: Business Location, an SGLN Digital Link

from.description: events at or after this time, ISO 8601

more.description: further EPCIS query parameters as a query string

tools.name: trace
tools.description: Trace a Serial, Lot or container through the repository as the signed-in user. backward: what it was made from (the TransformationEvents that output it, then their inputs, level by level) and the container it was packed in; forward: what was made from it and what it was packed into, down to where each result was last seen. Every step names its eventID, Read Point and time. A Lot is class level (/10/), a Serial or SSCC instance level. A returnable asset (GRAI, /8003/) or an individual asset (GIAI, /8004/), such as a minecart, a pack donkey or a bottle, answers what it carries now (every ADD minus every DELETE of the AggregationEvents it is the parent of), where it was last seen and its latest events.

identifier.description: the identifier, a GS1 Digital Link (01, 00, 8003, 8004) or EPC URN

tools.name: urnToDigitalLink
tools.description: Convert a legacy EPC URN (urn:epc:id:sgtin:0614141.107346.2017) into the preferred GS1 Digital Link URI form. Use this whenever you have a URN but want to emit a Digital Link, rather than assembling the URI by hand.

tools.name: validateCbvTerm
tools.description:
Check whether a value is a standard CBV term for an EPCIS event field, before putting it
in a document. Returns VALID, or NOT STANDARD with the nearest standard term when the
value is a known near-miss.

Use this whenever you are not certain of a term. EPCIS 2.0 JSON requires the bare short
name (`shipping`), never the EPCIS 1.x URN (`urn:epcglobal:cbv:bizstep:shipping`) and
never the CBV URI (`https://ref.gs1.org/cbv/BizStep-shipping`) — all three are checked
here and only the first is accepted.

field.description: The event field: bizStep, disposition, bizTransactionType, sourceType/destinationType

value.description: The value you intend to use, e.g. "shipping"

tools.name: validateEpcisDocument
tools.description:
Check an EPCIS 2.0 JSON document against the GS1 schema AND the OpenEPCIS rules — the
same two validators the capture endpoint runs. Call this on every document you produce,
before you present it; a document that fails here will be rejected on capture.

Reports the two layers separately, because they are different properties: the schema
permits things that are wrong in this architecture, such as `ilmd` on a serialised item.

Repairs are listed as things for YOU to fix, not applied. A document that needed a repair
is a document whose shape was wrong.

tools.name: validateIdentifier
tools.description: Check whether a GS1 identifier is valid, including its mod-10 check digit. Accepts a GS1 Digital Link URI (https://id.gs1.org/01/09521000002159/21/SER-1) or an EPC URN (urn:epc:id:sgtin:...). Use this before putting any identifier into an EPCIS document. Never guess a check digit and never derive a new identifier by changing a digit of an existing one — ask this tool instead.

identifier.description: A GS1 Digital Link URI or EPC URN

tools.name: verify_credential
tools.description: Verify a Verifiable Credential (JSON-LD with a Data Integrity proof, a VC-JOSE compact JWS or an SD-JWT VC) with the platform's verifier: signature, issuer DID and key, status (revoked or suspended) and the trust of the issuer. Answers valid true or false with the stage-by-stage verdict. The credential is sent to the verifier as given; nothing is stored.

credential.description: the credential: a JSON-LD object as JSON text, a compact JWS or an SD-JWT

profile.description: trust profile: self (default), untp, gs1 or espr-authority
